mechanism_name: SOL relative ticket-mix fragmentation continuation (majors-deflated average-trade-size breadth)
mechanism_story: Who is slow to react: the small-ticket retail crowd. Why the effect exists: information about an alt move reaches the retail long tail with a multi-day lag and arrives person-by-person — each newly-notified participant submits their own small marketable order on their own clock, so a retail attention episode diffuses SEQUENTIALLY over several days rather than printing at once. The footprint of that cohort is a fragmented ticket mix: elevated trade COUNT per unit of traded DOLLARS (small average ticket), which is a participation-MIX signature, not an aggressor-direction, large-trade, price-impact or raw-volume-level signature. Crucially the anchor conditions only on the SOL-SPECIFIC component: SOL's average ticket relative to its own trailing norm, deflated by the majors' (BTC+ETH pooled) same ratio. r_t < 1 means SOL's participation is fragmenting relative to BTC/ETH's own mix — SOL-specific retail attention mid-diffusion, not a market-wide microstructure shift — and the sequential arrival of small orders carries net inbound pressure into subsequent days, producing next-day continuation. The observable is exactly that: daily average ticket q̄ = quote_total/n_trades per symbol, ratio-of-ratios against 60-day trailing medians. When it must fail: (i) when fragmentation is market-wide the majors' deflation drives r_t toward 1 and the book stands aside (self-protecting); (ii) the fatal regime is saturation — the crowd fully arrived (fragmentation persistently deep with no further new entrants), after which small-ticket flow is exit liquidity for early holders and next-day drift dies and inverts; the same inversion occurs when small tickets reflect withdrawalling market-maker depth rather than arriving retail (mix identical, sign opposite); (iii) cost domination: if per-hold continuation is below the tier-2.0 round trip the book dies even while the drift exists. Novelty posture (measured, not argued, at D2): the conditioning series is a scale-free participation-mix ratio, deliberately double-normalised (own 60-day median, then majors' ratio) to strip common activity shocks; it contains no return, aggressor-split, large-trade-threshold, price-impact or raw-level term, so it is not a re-label of any packet section 4 family at any clock; the closest dead relatives are the liquidity-level family (Amihud/dollar-volume), against which pooled |rho| is measured at D2 and the veto accepted in advance.
universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT (the 3-symbol panel; SOLUSDT is the only traded symbol, BTCUSDT+ETHUSDT enter solely as the majors' ticket-mix deflator)
clock: daily (decision at the UTC 00:00 day boundary; daily-or-slower per axis-2 grant)
warmup: 61 daily decisions for the anchor (60-completed-day median burn-in + 1 completed day of ticket input); 121 for the neighbour (120-day median). No decision is emitted, and no position held, before the warmup completes inside each fold.
features_and_lags: Inputs (section 2 columns only): quote_total and n_trades for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT at H1 grain, aggregated to UTC days: Q_SYM(d) = SUM(quote_total) and N_SYM(d) = SUM(n_trades) over rows with symbol=SYM, day_utc=d. Availability law: the decision at 00:00 UTC of day t uses ONLY rows with close_ts <= t, i.e. completed days only — day t-1 for the current q̄ values and the trailing 60 completed days t-60..t-1 for the medians; no same-day rows enter the decision. All fills are explicitly next-bucket-open (day t bucket-0 VWAP, close_ts 01:00 UTC), so no same-bucket close is ever consumed by a fill decision.
entry_exit_fills: Entry: at decision t, if the anchor state is ON (r_{t-1} < 0.97), buy 1.0x notional SOLUSDT perp at day t bucket-0 VWAP (close_ts 01:00 UTC); else hold flat. Exit/holding: position held until the state turns OFF; with H=1 every day re-decides at 00:00, and an OFF decision closes the position at that day's bucket-0 VWAP; an unchanged state triggers NO fill (hold-through). Force-flat: any position still open at the final decision of a fold is closed at that fold's last tradable H1 bucket VWAP (the bucket whose close_ts equals the fold's last day boundary); no position ever crosses a fold boundary or the +/-1-day purge gap. Fill timing: every fill (entry and exit) is a taker fill at the H1 bucket-0 VWAP following the decision instant — the explicitly next-bucket-open default; no same-bucket close peeking.
costs: Acknowledged: taker fee is charged EXACTLY ONCE PER FILL (L-V14-0) — each entry and each exit is one fill, one fee; no maker assumptions, no fee netting, no intra-bucket averaging of fees. Cost book: TIER 2.0 IS THE PRIMARY BOOK (fee 5.0 bps x 2.0 = 10.0 bps per fill, slip floor 2 ticks); tiers x1.0 and x1.5 are reported as sensitivity only. Stress multipliers apply to BOOKED PnL.
anchor: Daily long/flat book on SOLUSDT. At each UTC 00:00 decision t in S0 (after warmup): (1) q̄_SOL(t-1) = Q_SOL(t-1)/N_SOL(t-1); q̄_MAJ(t-1) = (Q_BTC(t-1)+Q_ETH(t-1))/(N_BTC(t-1)+N_ETH(t-1)); (2) r_{t-1} = [ q̄_SOL(t-1)/med60(q̄_SOL)(t) ] / [ q̄_MAJ(t-1)/med60(q̄_MAJ)(t) ], where med60(q̄)(t) = median of the daily q̄ series over completed days t-60..t-1; (3) if r_{t-1} < 0.97, long 1.0x notional SOLUSDT perp, else flat. State changes execute as taker fills at day t bucket-0 VWAP per entry_exit_fills. Frozen parameters: 60-day median windows, entry threshold 0.97, hold H=1 day, long-only, no leverage scaling.
neighbour: Same mechanism, different frozen parameters: median windows med120 (trailing 120 completed days) for both numerator and denominator baselines, entry threshold r < 1.00, minimum hold 3 days — a position exits only at a decision where the state is OFF AND the position has been held for >= 3 complete UTC days; all else identical (same columns, same lag law, same fills, same force-flat). Tests robustness of the ticket-breadth effect to baseline horizon, threshold, and holding period without re-tuning anything else.
control: Exposure-form control (the packet's named control class for characteristic books): the characteristic is replaced by its RAW LEVEL. Identical book in every respect, except the conditioning variable r_{t-1} < 0.97 is replaced by the raw activity-level ratio v_{t-1} = Q_SOL(t-1)/med60(Q_SOL)(t) > 1.0 — long SOLUSDT whenever SOL's raw dollar volume is above its trailing median. This is the convenient explanation that must NOT reproduce the anchor: 'any activity elevation, not the ticket-mix characteristic, drives the drift'. If the raw-level book earns the anchor's expectancy, the participation-mix story is fake — the edge was just SOL activity level (itself adjacent to the dead dollar-volume family), and the family dies. Control decision/fill/cost machinery is byte-identical to the anchor's.
exposure_series_spec: Daily conditioning exposure series for D2 (exact formula over panel columns): r_t = [ q̄_SOL(t-1)/med60(q̄_SOL)(t) ] / [ q̄_MAJ(t-1)/med60(q̄_MAJ)(t) ], with q̄_SOL(t-1) = SUM(quote_total)/SUM(n_trades) over SOLUSDT H1 rows of day t-1; q̄_MAJ(t-1) = (SUM(quote_total,BTC)+SUM(quote_total,ETH))/(SUM(n_trades,BTC)+SUM(n_trades,ETH)) over day t-1; med60(·)(t) = median of the corresponding daily series over completed days t-60..t-1; one value per UTC decision day t in S0 (the value dated t reflects day t-1 information only). D2 pools r_t (and the neighbour variant with med120 windows) against the full forbidden-inventory exposure set; pooled |rho| <= 0.20 required.
falsification_rule: Pre-registered and mechanical; the family DIES if ANY of: (F1) G11 — the exposure-form control (raw dollar-volume level book) reproduces the anchor on pooled S0 after tier-2.0 costs: same expectancy sign AND |control expectancy| >= 0.5 x |anchor expectancy|; (F2) anchor G1: pooled after-cost expectancy <= 0 at tier 2.0; (F3) D2 novelty veto: pooled |rho| > 0.20 between the exposure series r_t (anchor and neighbour variants as specified) and ANY forbidden-inventory conditioning exposure (the Amihud/ILLIQ, dollar-volume-shock and LIQEPIS members are the a-priori closest and are accepted as legitimate kills); (F4) anchor G2: pooled PF < 1.10. No re-thresholding, re-windowing, re-clocking, majors-reference swap, sign-flip or symbol-subset rescue is permitted after any F fires; a dead family is dead at every parameterisation of this mechanism.
expected_failure_interpretation: A REJECT means SOL's ticket-mix fragmentation is not a mid-diffusion marker of staggered retail arrival. Specifically: F1 implies the drift is explained by raw activity level alone — the mix characteristic added nothing, and the edge (if any) belongs to the already-dead activity-level family; F2/F4 imply sequential retail arrival is too weak or too slow to clear taker costs at tier 2.0; F3 implies the ratio-of-ratios is statistically the dead liquidity/size exposures (the a-priori most likely novelty kill, accepted in advance). In every case the conclusion is that WHO trades SOL (ticket breadth) has no incremental after-cost information beyond what dead families already encode; the family is closed at all baselines, thresholds, clocks and symbol subsets.
expected_failure_mode: Cost domination (the named risk of this frontier). Turnover estimate per decision: the long/flat state is slower than P1's (crossings of a ratio-of-ratios around 1 against long median windows), est. 18-30 state changes per 365 decisions = 0.05-0.08 changes per decision-day, each change = 1 exit + 1 entry taker fill, i.e. ~0.10-0.16 taker fills per decision-day (~36-60 fills per S0 year, average hold ~5-8 days). At tier 2.0 (10.0 bps per fill + 2-tick slip floor) that is ~3.6-6.0% annual cost drag at full notional, so each completed hold must gross >= ~25-30 bps (>= ~4-5 bps per held day) to survive; if the retail-diffusion drift is thinner than that, the book dies by cost domination before any statistical verdict is reachable. This is the primary expected failure mode.
